title: Sung Tieu
subtitle: Inserzioni
body:
Now in its third edition, Inserzioni confirms its role as a permanent laboratory at Castello di Rivoli. Conceived as an invitation for contemporary artists to engage with the castle's unfinished architecture and its collection displays, the project periodically transforms the museum’s permanent collection presentations into an ever-evolving exhibition.

The commission by Sung Tieu (Hải Dương, Vietnam, 1987) forms part of the research the artist developed for the German Pavilion at the 61st International Art Exhibition of La Biennale di Venezia (2026) titled In Minor Keys. There Tieu transformed the architecture that has housed Germany’s national participation in the Giardini since 1905 into a GDR ruin, covering its façade in more than three million mosaic tesserae based on the Plattenbauten, the prefabricated concrete blocks of East Germany. One such building, in particular Gehrenseestrasse in former East Berlin, housed Vietnamese contract workers, many of whom had come to the GDR under bilateral labour agreements. It was also the artist's childhood home.

At Castello di Rivoli, the work takes on a new dimension in Room 18. An immersive environment clad in mosaics frames a trompe l'oeil depiction of the building's corridor, illuminated by a monochromatic yellow light inspired by the lighting of German Autobahns. This artificial illumination radically transforms the perception of colour, atmosphere and space.

Through elements belonging both to personal memory and to urban history, Tieu constructs an experience in which architecture becomes the place where dynamics of control, marginalisation, and belonging are manifested. The exhibition space is not merely a container for the work, but a perceptual device that makes visible the often invisible forms through which contemporary society determines who can inhabit a place, under what conditions, and according to which power relations.

This project is curated by Francesco Manacorda and co-commissioned by The Shen Foundation and the Castello di Rivoli Museo d'Arte Contemporanea.

See the Castello di Rivoli Museo d'Arte Contemporanea's website for more information.
